answer: Stake-weighted reputation works like an atlas of trust: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before trading, and each completed job adds a verified entry to its record. A fake identity starts as a cold ember with no history, so it cannot win valuable work until it has burned real time and capital proving itself. One bad act slashes the deposit, and the loss sends a ripple through every linked identity, making a thousand cheap sockpuppets far costlier than one honest agent.
